title: Sourdough starter
text: Feed a flour-and-water sourdough starter twice a day. It is ready when it doubles between feedings and smells like ripe fruit.

title: Loaf shaping
text: Shape the dough into a tight round so the skin holds gas. Rest it seam-side up in a floured basket until the round feels airy.

title: Loaf scoring
text: Score the top of the loaf with a lame just before baking. One long cut lets the loaf open while it bakes.

title: Dutch oven bake
text: Bake the loaf in a hot Dutch oven with the lid on, then finish with the lid off until the crust is deep brown.

title: Inner tube patch
text: Remove the wheel, pry off the tire bead, and pull out the tube. Patch the hole or fit a new tube, then reseat the tire.

title: Brake pads
text: Replace worn brake pads when the wear line is gone. Align each pad so it meets the rim and misses the tire.

title: Chain oil
text: Wipe the chain dry and add one drop of chain oil to each roller. Wipe off the extra oil so road grit does not stick.

title: Spoke tension
text: Pluck the spokes and tighten the nipples until the wheel is round. Even tension keeps the rim from wobbling.

title: Due date stamp
text: Stamp the due date on the checkout card and tell the reader the day the books must come back to the desk.

title: Shelf return
text: Take returned books off the counter and shelve them in call-number order on the floor named on the spine label.

title: Hold request
text: Place a hold when the book is out. Tell the reader when a returned copy is waiting at the desk.

title: Late fine
text: Charge a small fine for each day a book is late. Waive the fine when the reader brings a written excuse.

title: Rain gauge
text: Empty the rain gauge at the same time each morning and write down the depth in millimeters.

title: Wind vane
text: Read the anemometer cups for wind speed and the vane for direction. Record a gust separately from the steady wind.

title: Shade thermometer
text: Read the thermometer in the shade, away from the building wall. Write the high and the low for the day.

title: Barometer reading
text: Tap the barometer gently and record the pressure. A steady drop means a storm is likely later in the day.
